title: Components Are Functions
summary: UI as a function of data: props, composition, children and keys.

steps.title: UI = f(data)
body: React's central idea: a **component** is a function that takes data (**props**) and returns a description of the UI. You never "go and change the button"; you change the data and React calls your function again.
type ButtonProps = { label: string; disabled?: boolean };
function Button({ label, disabled = false }: ButtonProps) {

The `<button>` syntax is **JSX** (lesson 3). Our exercises cannot run JSX, so they write components as plain functions returning HTML strings. The thinking is identical: props in, markup out, no side effects.

steps.explain: Keys must be **stable** and **unique** among siblings. Random keys remount every item on every render.

steps.prompt: Components as plain functions: what does this print?
code:
const Item = ({ name, unread }: { name: string; unread: number }) => `
  • ${name}${Badge({ n: unread })}
    • `;
const Inbox = ({ items }: { items: { name: string; unread: number }[] }) =>
console.log(Inbox({ items: [{ name: "Work", unread: 2 }, { name: "Home", unread: 0 }] }));
steps.explain: Each component only knows its own props. `Inbox` composes `Item`, which composes `Badge`.
